data: Introduction to Sociological and Anthropological Thought

This required course introduces students to key moments in the development of sociological and
anthropological thought. Starting with the origins of the two disciplines; the ways in which both
disciplines are from inception implicated in the social, historical, political and economic context
out of which they emerged; we proceed to examine how ideas have emerged over time, through
relentless critical inquiry and engagement with diverse and changing contexts. Each module will
introduce students to a particular moment in the discourse and involve engagement with a
selection of representative texts drawn from key sociological and anthropological thinkers. This
is not an exhaustive course on the history of sociological/anthropological thought, nevertheless
the representative selection of texts is aimed at elucidating key theoretical insights of important


thinkers. Students are expected to undertake immersive reading and critically reflect on the ideas
thus introduced and their relevance (or not) in the contemporary world.
Assistant Professor, Sociology and Social Anthropology
